newsitem.title: KENYA: Turnover up, share index eases at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Turnover up, share index eases at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Turnover rose at the Nairobi Stock Exchange boosted by sustained foreign demand, but the share index eased slightly, bourse officials said.
The Nairobi bourse 20-share index eased 0.39 points to close at 3448.69. Turnover was posted at 31.821 million shillings on 570,781 shares from 11.567 million shillings on 311,830 shares.
Brokers who had forecast the market would be unable to sustain prices at the level of the past two weeks said that the index would continue to drop until it found an equilibrium point.

"Most speculators are confused now that the market is stabilising because they thought they would make a quick kill. But foreign investors are still buying because they buy for the long term," a broker told Reuters.
Foreign investors bought some 120,000 shares of Kakuzi at 100 from 98 and 133,000 shares of Firestone East Africa at 33 from 30 on the three-day special board.
A bourse official said the rest of the day's trading at the bourse was retail, concentrated in small lots.
Barclays Bank shed a shilling to close at 114, while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 55 from 58.
National Bank of Kenya eased to 15 from 15.55 while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 36.50 from 38.
"A lot of cautious trading is going on. Brokers do not want to lay it all on the table -- they're doing a lot of 'testing the water' kind of trading," a senior bourse official said.
National Carrier Kenya Airways traded at 8.60 from 8.55 while Bamburi Cement eased to 40 from 40.25.
